dena: Quick heads-up — after the int8 bring-up for m-embed-compact we see a weird translation-anchoring shift. Spanish/French queries are drifting out of English clusters but float16 baseline is fine. Reproducer below, trying to figure out if it's quantization or dataset drift.
ryan: Can you drop the metrics you saw? recall@1/5 maybe?
dena: Here are the small-run numbers from the validation holdout (same examples across langs):
```
model: m-embed-compact-int8
lang: en/es/fr
recall@1: en: 0.82 / es: 0.61 / fr: 0.63
recall@5: en: 0.94 / es: 0.78 / fr: 0.79
cluster_purity(lang-centroids): en: 0.88 / es: 0.62 / fr: 0.64
baseline float16 recall@1 (same set): en:0.83 es:0.81 fr:0.80
```
sophia: Yikes, that gap for es/fr is too big to be sampling noise. float16 looks fine so likely quantization artifacts. Did you use per-channel or per-tensor quant?
dena: per-tensor symmetric with static calibration using heldout. Used typical calibration batch (10k examples). Also tried 6-bit and results are slightly better but still gap.
liam: Could be embedding norm collapse for non-en tokens. Any shift in norm distributions pre/post quant?
dena: Quick norm check attached: mean L2 norms pre-quant [en:1.02 es:0.98 fr:0.99], post-int8 [en:1.01 es:0.74 fr:0.77]. So es/fr lost magnitude.
ryan: That smells like scale clipping in embedding matmul or an activation quant mismatch. Did we fold layernorm differently in the int8 path?
sophia: Also try running output-centering (subtract mean) before comparison as a sanity check; if it fixes recall it's magnitude shift.
dena: Did the centering trick on a sample — recall@1 for es jumped to 0.78, fr to 0.77 (int8). So magnitude is the main factor.
liam: Nice. For a fix: try per-channel quant or recalibrate with lang-balanced calibration set. Also enable mixed-precision on final projection layer.
sophia: Agree. Perf hit might be small if only final proj stays fp16. Can you run a quick ablation: per-channel q + fp16 proj + lang-balanced calib?
dena: Kicked off a job: run id embed/1738889999/ablate-1. Will post results. ETA ~30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
evalbot: Scheduled run complete: run id embed/1738889999/ablate-1 — results attached. Summary: per-channel + fp16-proj + lang-balanced calib closes ~90% of gap, recall@1 es=0.80 fr=0.79.
ryan: That's promising. Can you add a small regression test to the onboarding pipeline (lang stratified recall thresholds) so future quant builds catch this?
dena: Yep adding a gated test + note in the quant runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbook/quant-embed#translation-anchoring. Filing ticket ML-523 to roll fix and retest canary.
sophia: Thx. Also add a short paragraph in the model card about per-channel being required for multilingual compaction.
dena: Will do. Follow-ups: 1) patch quant config, 2) run full holdout (100k) before canary. Assigning: dena (patch & tests), ryan (canary infra), liam (calib scripts).
liam: Got it.
ryan: :thumbsup: keep us posted, flag any perf regression.
dena: will update thread when full holdout finishes. :eyes:
